subject: Information Theory
title: LDPC Codes
description: A quick, practical guide to LDPC Codes.

hook.text: Robert Gallager invented LDPC codes in his 1960 PhD thesis. They were ignored for 30 years, then revolutionized 5G.

buildup.text: LDPC (low-density parity-check) codes have sparse parity-check matrices. Most entries are zero.

discovery.text: The sparsity enables belief propagation decoding: messages pass along a graph, iteratively refining bit estimates.

twist.text: LDPC codes can be designed to approach Shannon's limit within hundredths of a decibel. They're practically optimal.

climax.text: 5G NR, Wi-Fi 6, DVB-S2, and 10 Gigabit Ethernet all use LDPC codes. Gallager's thesis finally won.

punchline.text: Ignored for 30 years. Now in every phone and router.

quiz.question: Why were LDPC codes ignored and then rediscovered?
options: 1960s computers couldn't handle the decoding; modern hardware can
